rulings.note: Sunwatch Knight: 'watch' reads as vigilance-flavor for an ETB vigilance-granter; Knight (12) beats Human Soldier oversaturation. Tireless Chaplain was close runner-up.
Living Grafter nails the 'spells that target your creatures add counters' via the graft pun; Elf Druid options both fine on census, Beast (D) misreads the support role.

Vanishing Act is the cleanest exile-then-return pun and avoids echoing the pool's existing flicker cards (Cloudshift, Otherworldly Journey) in wording. A/B are literal duplicates of each other — flag.

Skybound Tactician most directly frames a flying-anthem; kept off 'Skyward' to avoid a near-duplicate with the RW_2-1 pool option of the same name, and off Human Soldier (D) to dodge further Human bloat.
Wayclearer Knight is the only option that literally describes tapping down a blocker on attack; accepted the Human tag as the cost of a much sharper mechanic read.
Ambuscade (ambush/surprise) ties flash-matters neatly; picked the plain-Wizard typeline over Human Wizard. B and C are identical options — coin flip.
Surgecaster distinguishes this UR flash-counters twin from the WU one (Ambuscade Adept) without reusing wording; Wildspark Elemental undersells the wizard identity.
Updraft is a clean, literal wind-lifts-you-into-flight image with zero pool collision. A/B duplicate.
Undertow Recall covers both halves of the effect (recall=bounce, undertow=pull back/current=draw) and reads distinctly U; 'Withdrawal' options undersell the draw half.

Grovecaller Adept, tribes Elf+Wizard — typeline mirrors the chosen tribes coherently (G=Elf, U=Wizard), both mid-census and non-Human. Hybrid Cultivator's 'hybrid' risks confusion with the hybrid-mana term.
Curious Faerie is a near-literal 'draw more, grow' pun; Faerie (3) is on-brand for U whimsy and avoids introducing a new Fish tribe or thinly-populated Merfolk-only flavor.
Arcane Drifter ties 'noncreature spell' (arcane) to the conditional-flight payoff (drifter) cleanly; Riftwing options crowd the pool's existing 'Illusion Drake.'

Nightwatch Seer frames the opponent's-turn instant-speed trigger well. Ledger Bulwark is a clever pun (tracks casts) but Wall implies Defender, which isn't in the card's stated design; safer to skip it.
Chrysalis Ward captures both halves — a growing protective shell for the toughness bump and hexproof. C/D duplicate ('Shielding Current').
Groundwaker is the most literal 'land wakes into a creature' read; plain Druid keeps typeline unforced versus introducing Dryad.

Landbound Warden covers both the land-theme and the vigilance-granting guardian role without the free Reach that Treefolk (A/C/D) would silently add via implied keywords — that ability isn't in the card's stated text.
Thriving Elemental is accurate to an any-creature (not tribal) go-wide payoff; Packmother/Kindred Whelp falsely imply a Beast/Wolf-only restriction the card doesn't have.
Bloomrot Shaman puns death-into-growth as tightly as Deathbloom but sidesteps 'Deathbloom' as an overworked Golgari cliché term; Human Cleric (D) also unnecessarily adds to Human count.

Kindling Executioner covers both halves (kindling=fuel/damage, executioner=sacrifice) slightly more completely than Altar Butcher's sacrifice-only focus; Goblin Cannoneer misses the sac-outlet half entirely.
Feral Conduit's 'channel' image is the only option that actually describes amplifying every spell you cast; mild echo of the pool's 'Tidal Conduit' but no direct overlap in register or word order.
Warcry Zealot captures the rally-off-others'-attacks trigger cleanly; accepted introducing Berserker as a fresh singleton subtype since it's genre-standard for red aggro.
Loamkin Sprout triple-puns land+kinship+growth; picked over the equally strong Frontier Sapling for a fresher root word with the same fit.
Cinderfed Giant's 'fed' verb is the only option that literally frames growing from repeated burn-sorcery casts; Giant (2) is a light, appropriate big-body tag.
Slagstrike is as vivid as Scrap the Machine for artifact removal but carries zero pool collision, versus Scrap the Machine's mild echo of the pool's 'Scrap Hound.'
Fuse-Lit Goblin's lit-fuse image is a precise 1:1 metaphor for 'activate an ability → triggered damage'; kept the Goblin typeline consistent with this pool's dominant red identity over Human Rogue.
Timberland Strider's direct land callout best matches the landfall pump trigger; Elf Scout introduces Scout as a new but genre-standard subtype.
Watchful Grace pairs 'watchful' (vigilance) with 'grace' (the blessing bestowed via spellcasting) elegantly; Spirit avoids the redundant name-echoes-type pattern of the Cleric options.
Renewed Stand covers untap+vigilance as cleanly as 'Second Wind' but avoids that phrase's status as a very common refresh-effect idiom across other games. B/C duplicate.

Design explicitly calls for a POPULOUS chosen tribe — Human (62) dwarfs Knight (12), so A/B (Knight) are functionally weak. Fervent Adherent takes Human as the ability-tribe while keeping the card's own typeline Cleric, satisfying the populous requirement without adding another Human creature to an already-saturated pool.
Banner of the Vanguard uses the classic anthem-effect symbol (banner) cleanly; avoided Warhorn Rallier for its word-stem overlap with the pool's existing 'Rally the Troops.'

Windcall Seraph covers both the trigger (casting=calling) and the effect (flight=wind) more completely than Skyraising Angel's effect-only framing; Angel typeline is consistent since the card already has Flying as stated text.
Triage Cleric's 'treat casualties in order of severity' precisely frames lifegain triggered by other creatures' ETB damage; Convalescent Firebrand mixes healer/aggressor connotations awkwardly.

batchNotes:
Overall the 32 picks skew toward precise, single/double-word mechanic puns (Updraft, Slagstrike, Chrysalis Ward, Loamkin Sprout, Cinderfed Giant) and hold the line on the Human-oversaturation warning — only 2 new Human-typed creatures were added (Wayclearer Knight, Banner of the Vanguard) out of 32, both accepted because their mechanic-fit was clearly best-in-slot, and RW_0-1's populous-tribe requirement was satisfied by choosing Human as the *ability* target rather than the creature's own type. Two implied-keyword traps were dodged deliberately: GU_1-2's Wall option (free Defender not in the card's text) and GW_1-2's three Treefolk options (free Reach not in the card's text).

Biggest set-level imbalance: Elemental typeline was picked 4 times (Landbound Warden, Thriving Elemental, Feral Conduit, Loamkin Sprout) against a census baseline of only 5 existing Elementals — nearly doubling that tribe in one batch, each individually justified (neutral, non-tribal-implying, on-color) but collectively worth a rebalancing look; RG_2-2 or GW_1-2 could take a Beast/other pick instead if diversity is prioritized over per-card optimality. Beast, despite being well-established (11) and offered as a strong option on at least three cards (GW_3-1, RG_2-2, GW_2-1), was never selected — another possible rebalance target. Two brand-new singleton subtypes were introduced (Berserker for Warcry Zealot, Scout for Timberland Strider); both are genre-standard enough to read as natural rather than forced. Minor word-repetition: 'Adept' appears twice (Grovecaller Adept, Ambuscade Adept) and 'Ward/Warden' twice (Chrysalis Ward, Landbound Warden) — neither is a true collision, just a light echo worth knowing about. No exact name collisions survive within the picked set or against pool names; the closest calls (Feral Conduit vs. pool's Tidal Conduit, Fuse-Lit Goblin vs. Ambush Djinn-adjacent space) were accepted as same-genre-different-word, not true duplicates.
